2. Only the times 7, 8, 9 exist, and "before" is strict. Three strictly increasing start times must use 7, 8, 9 in that order, so **R = 7 P.M., W = 8 P.M., H = 9 P.M.**
3. W is at 8 P.M., so W is the only movie on screen 3. This satisfies "sci-fi is not on screen 3."
4. R is at 7 P.M. on screen 1 or 2. Romance is not on screen 2, so **R is on screen 1 at 7 P.M.**
5. The remaining slots are: screen 1 at 9 P.M., screen 2 at 7 P.M., and screen 2 at 9 P.M. H (at 9 P.M.) takes screen 1 or screen 2 at 9 P.M. M and H must be on different screens.
   - **Case 1:** H = S1 at 9. Then M is on screen 2, and sci-fi (S) takes the other screen-2 slot. Schedules: S2 = (M@7, S@9) or (S@7, M@9).
   - **Case 2:** H = S2 at 9. Then M = S1 at 9, and S = S2 at 7.

   This gives three complete schedules, and each one satisfies all the original constraints:
   - (i) S1: R@7, H@9; S2: M@7, S@9
   - (ii) S1: R@7, H@9; S2: S@7, M@9
   - (iii) S1: R@7, M@9; S2: S@7, H@9

**Checking the options across the schedules**

- A (horror on screen 1): true in (i), (ii); false in (iii). Not necessary.
- B (mystery begins at 7): true in (i); false in (ii). Not necessary.
- C (mystery on screen 2): false in (iii). Not necessary.
- D (sci-fi begins at 9): true in (i); false in (ii), (iii). Not necessary.
